case.subject: Product meeting
case.title: Sprint planning: onboarding scope and owners

canvasName: R3-C02 Sprint planning: onboarding scope and owners

segments.text: Let's start the sprint planning meeting. We have a five person product team and two weeks. The goal for this sprint is to ship the new onboarding flow to a small group of beta users, not to finish everything on the backlog. Please keep that goal in mind when we discuss scope. I want us to leave with a committed set of stories, one owner for each, the dependencies, and the risks we accept. First, the business context.

segments.text: Last month only thirty eight percent of new users completed onboarding. The biggest drop off is at the workspace setup step, where people do not understand whether they need to invite their team right away. Support gets about twenty tickets a week about that screen.
segments.textReply: Added the onboarding baseline and primary friction point, plus the sprint’s two-week, five-person beta-scope guardrail.

Story two, add a progress checklist after signup. That is four frontend days, plus analytics, plus two backend days if we want to remember checklist state. shapes.title: Sprint planning summary · onboarding beta
shapes.html:
Sprint planning · Onboarding beta
Purpose: commit a small, measurable onboarding beta slice—not finish the backlog. Baseline completion is 38%; workspace setup is the main drop-off (~20 support tickets/week).
Consensus scope & decisions
  • Story 1: shorten setup from 4 steps to 2; invitation optional. Ship to beta.
  • Story 4: capture only 3 events—signup started, workspace created, invite sent. Dashboard is a saved SQL view; no new UI.
  • Story 5: fix invitation email bug if support reproduction is found; otherwise investigate only and do not claim shipped.
  • Story 3: import technical design + migration dependency ticket only; no UI this sprint.
  • Story 2: checklist deferred one sprint; keep design ready and put it at top of next sprint backlog.
  • Fixed work: consent screen and mobile API field. Capacity: 16 developer-days.
Compact timeline
Week 1 · 4 workdays
Mon–Wed: Story 1 implementation. Tue: support bug reproduction. Wed: consent screen + analytics start; legal review. Thu: bug fix if reproduced; analytics; Story 3 import design.
Week 2 · 5 workdays
Mon: stabilize staging. Tue: mobile API field; QA starts after staging is stable. Tue–Wed: QA; Wed: mid-sprint review. Thu: beta rollout. Fri: buffer.
Release gate: if QA finds a blocker Tuesday, delay beta one week; never ship broken onboarding.
Actions · owners · deadlines
WorkOwner(s)Deadline / dependency
Story 1: shortened flow + backend flagPriya; Sam frontend review; Alex backend flagImplement Mon–Wed, week 1; 3 FE + 1 BE day
Story 5: invitation bug reproduction / fixAlex + Sam; Support supplies reproductionRepro Tue; if not found by Wed, investigate only; 1 day estimate
Story 4: 3 events + saved SQL viewDiego; Alex contributes ½ dayEvents Wed–Thu, week 1; 2 days Diego + ½ day Alex
Consent screenMei + PriyaWednesday legal review; due end of week 1; 1 FE day + ½ review
Mobile API fieldAlexShip Tuesday, week 2; ½ backend day
Story 3 import technical design + migration dependencyOwner not explicitly assigned; migration is Diego-ownedThursday, week 1; migration blocked by two legacy tables; no UI
Tickets, unestimated work, summary postAll owners; meeting lead posts summaryUpdate tickets by end of day; flag unestimated work; post to sprint channel today
Accepted risks & safeguards
  • Accept checklist delay of one sprint; shorter flow may recover enough activation.
  • Do not ship both flow changes untested; QA has only 3 days.
  • Migration is late and blocked by two legacy tables; avoid partial import UI.
  • QA starts only when staging is stable. Any Tuesday blocker delays beta one week.
  • Story 5 race condition is suspected; without reproduction by Wednesday, do not report a fix as shipped.
Open follow-ups
  • Confirm all ticket estimates, especially Story 3 design/dependency work; flag unestimated tasks.
  • Ensure legal review occurs Wednesday and support reproduction arrives Tuesday.
  • Confirm staging stability before QA begins; beta decision follows QA results.
  • Next check-in: Monday standup. Mid-sprint review: Wednesday, week 2.
